body.p: At the outset, the Examiner is thanked for the review and consideration of the pending application. The Office Action has been received and its contents reviewed.

The above amendments are made in response to the Office Action of October 8, 2024. Claims 1, 4-7, 11, and 13 have been amended, and claims 2, 3, 10, 14, and 15 have been canceled without prejudice in this submission. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the claims, the specification, and the drawings as originally filed. The present amendment introduces no new matter.
Claims 1, 4-9, and 11-13 are pending in the present application upon entry of the amendment. Claims 1 and 13 are independent.

Applicant reserves the right to pursue the original claims in this and in any other applications. The Examiner's reconsideration is respectfully requested in view of the above amendments and the following remarks.

The disclosure is objected because in the opening paragraph, the priority information is not listed. The address the issue, Applicant has added a new paragraph [0000] to list the priority information. No new matter is added in this amendment. Accordingly, withdrawal of the objection is respectfully requested.

The Office Action indicates that claim limitation(s) such as "control element" in Claims 1, 5, 11 and 13 and "measuring device" in Claim 13 are interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) or pre- paragraph AIA 35 U.S.C. 112 sixth, because the claim limitation(s) uses a generic placeholder that is coupled with functional language without reacting sufficient structure to perform the recited function and the generic placeholder is not preceded by a structure modifier.
1. With respect to the "control element" as recited in Claims 1, 5, 11 and 13, it is respectfully
submitted that a person of ordinary skill in the art could have clearly understood and
conceived such a control element for controlling an optical path by reflecting light and

transmitting the reflected light, particularly, in light of the specification and the drawings of the present application. For example, a person of ordinary skill in the art could have clearly understood the descriptions in paragraph [0046] of the specification, with reference to FIGS.
1 to 3. Further, a person of ordinary skill in the art would consider the descriptions as a possible example (or non-limiting embodiment) for the detailed structure of the claimed
control element and could realize that such a control element as claimed can be implemented

application. As such, a person of ordinary skill in the art could also adopt any other suitable structures or configurations for the claimed control element. Therefore, the interpretation of

of the present application.
2. With respect to the "measuring device" as recited in the claims, it is respectfully submitted
that a person of ordinary skill in the art could have clearly understood and conceived such a
measuring device which measures a three-dimensional image, particularly, in light of the
specification and the drawings of the present application. For example, a person of ordinary
skill in the art could have clearly understood the descriptions in paragraph [0038] of the
specification, with reference to FIGS. 1 to 3. Further, a person of ordinary skill in the art
would consider the descriptions as a possible example (or non-limiting embodiment) for the
detailed structure of the claimed measuring device and could realize that such a measuring device as claimed can be implemented in various structures or manners without departing
from the descriptions of the present application. As such, a person of ordinary skill in the art
could also adopt any other suitable structures or configurations for the claimed measuring
device. Therefore, the interpretation of the limitation "measuring device" should not be
limited to the specification and the drawings of the present application.
Rejections of Claims under 35 U.S.C. @ 112(b)

Claim 7 is rejected under 35 U.S.C 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor regards as the invention. Specifically, the outstanding Office Action asserted that
"pattern unit" in Claim 7 would be interpreted under 35 U.S.C. 112(f) but there is no specification support as to what structure this corresponds to, accordingly, the term is unclear.

Without conceding the merits of the rejections, Claim 7 has been amended to recite "pattern generator." Paragraph [0060] of the specification describes that light is irradiated onto a "pattern unit" having a pattern formed thereon, and the pattern of the "pattern unit" is reflected in the irradiated light. A person of ordinary skill in the pertinent technology field would clearly understand from paragraph [0060] that the "pattern unit" is a "pattern generator" having a specific structure for generating a pattern in the irradiated light.
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C 112(b).
Rejections of Claims under 35 U.S.C. @@ 102 and 103

Claims 1-3, 5-7, and 9-15 have been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) as allegedly being anticipated by Fisker et al. (US 2012/0092461, hereinafter "Fisker"). Claim 4 has been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Fisker in view of Homan et al. (US 2020/0281660, hereinafter "Homan"). Claim 8 has been rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Fisker in view of Jian et al. (CN 110720986, hereinafter "Jian"). These rejections are respectfully traversed.

body.p: In the Office Action, independent claim 1 is rejected for being anticipated by Fisker. Applicant respectfully disagrees.

Fisker relates to a handheld scanner 100 that uses confocal pattern projection technology to measure the 3D geometric shape of part of a surface of an object. The handheld scanner 100 includes a light source 110, optics 120, pattern generation means 130, beam splitter 140, and an image sensor (camera) 180 (see FIG. 1 of Fisker as reproduced below).

Fisker requires acquiring multiple 2D images of a subject through a camera with respect to a focus plane that periodically and continuously varies due to a focusing element (e.g., a lens), thereby measuring the 3D shape. In other words, Fisker merely measures the 3D shape by periodically varying the focal plane, capturing multiple 2D images of the object (over a certain period), and using these images as a basis for the 3D shape measurement. The multiple 2D images of the object used by Fisker to measure the 3D shape are different from the "light field image in which a plurality of sub-images including color information and direction information of the reflected light are combined" as recited in amended Claim 1. Additionally, while Fisker discloses that color information can be registered for the scanned object (see paragraphs [0151]- [0158] of Fisker), this is different from the limitation "light field image in which a plurality of sub-images including color information and direction information of the reflected light are combined" as recited in amended Claim 1. Therefore, Fisker fails to disclose or suggest the limitations "the light field image of the object being an image in which a plurality of sub-images including color information and direction information of the reflected light are combined" and "measure a light intensity of reflected light at each of a plurality ofpoints constituting a surface of the object using the plurality of sub-images included in the light filed image of the object acquired through the light field camera; generate phase data based on the measured light intensity; generate a three-dimensional image of the surface of the object by calculating a height of each of the plurality ofpoints based on the generated phase data; and transmit the three- dimensional image of the surface of the object to an external electronic device through the communication circuit" as recited in amended Claim 1.

Furthermore, Fisker merely measures 3D shapes and does not generate a three- dimensional image for the specific purpose of matching with medical images. Therefore, Fisker does not disclose or suggest the limitation "wherein the three-dimensional image of the surface of the object is an image used for matching with a medical image of the object, and the medical image of the object is one of a CT image and an MRI image."
The other reference, Homan and Jian, fail to cure the deficiencies of Fisker. Neither Homan nor Jian discloses or suggests the above-mentioned limitations of amended Claim 1.

In light of the above reasons, Applicant respectfully submits that amended independent claim 1 is patentably distinct over and not obvious over Fisker, Homan, and Jian, either alone or in combination.

Independent Claim 13 has been amended to recite the similar limitations of amended Claim 1, and accordingly, amended Claim 13 is also patentably distinct over and not obvious over Fisker, Homan, and Jian, either alone or in combination, for the same reasons as discussed with respect to amended Claim 1.
Claims 4-9 and 11-12 directly or indirectly depend from independent Claim 1, thus
include all the limitations of amended Claim 1. Thus, claims 4-9 and 11-12 are believed to be allowable at least for the reasons given to the independent claims.
Accordingly, withdrawal of the rejections under 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 against all the pending claims is respectfully requested.

In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that the instant application is in condition for allowance. Accordingly, it is respectfully requested that this application be allowed and a Notice of Allowance issued.

If the Examiner believes that a telephone conference with Applicant's attorneys would be advantageous to the disposition of this case, the Examiner is cordially requested to telephone the undersigned.

In the event the Commissioner of Patents and Trademarks deems additional fees to be due in connection with this application, Applicant's attorney hereby authorizes that such fee be charged to Deposit Account No. 50-5622.
Respectfully submitted,
